title: Chocolate Hazelnut Gelato (Gianduja)
changes_from_base: Home-ground roasted hazelnut paste and Dutch cocoa replace the pistachio milk; no egg yolks, the base is set with cornflour.
summary: The flavour of the famous chocolate spread in a scoop: roasted hazelnuts ground to a runny paste and blended into a dark cocoa milk base.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Paste
steps.text: Blitz the hazelnuts in the processor, scraping down now and then, until they go from crumbs to a clump and finally a runny paste, 5-8 min; add the oil once the paste starts to loosen.

steps.title: Cocoa
steps.text: Whisk the cocoa, sugar, salt and cornflour together in the saucepan so the cocoa does not form lumps, then whisk in a splash of the milk to make a smooth paste.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Whisk in the rest of the milk and the cream, bring to a simmer and cook for 3 min, stirring, until it lightly coats the spatula.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Pour the hot chocolate milk into the processor with the hazelnut paste and blend until completely smooth.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Sieve into the bowl over iced water, pressing it through, stir until cool, then cover and chill for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pack into the container, cover the surface and freeze for at least 4 h. This gelato sets firm, so allow 15 min in the fridge before scooping.

tips: Be patient with the paste; it looks dry for several minutes before it suddenly turns runny.
Buy hazelnuts already roasted and skinned to save time, or roast at 180 °C for 10-12 min and rub off the skins.
Top with chopped toasted hazelnuts for crunch.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered with baking paper pressed on the surface in the freezer for up to 2 weeks. Soften for 10-15 min in the fridge before scooping.
